title: Capacity cliff incident follow-up: admission thresholds, soft-preemption, and graceful dropback
creator: Priya Sharma
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-08 we experienced a hosted API capacity cliff in eu-west-1 that caused a sustained backlog on several GPU pools for ~45 minutes and produced elevated 5xx rates and tail latencies for paying customers. This ticket tracks follow-ups from the postmortem: make admission/capacity behavior resilient to transient prewarm loss and noisy bursts, provide graceful degradation semantics (soft-preemption + dropback) for lower-priority work, and codify runbooks and observability for earlier detection.

Root cause (brief): a confluence of (1) simultaneous prewarm eviction during a rolling infra upgrade, (2) an admission window that allowed short-lived bursts to consume remaining credits, and (3) autoscaler cooldowns tuned for steady-state rather than sudden spikes. The result was a "capacity cliff": demand overwhelmed remaining machines and request backlog amplified due to lack of graceful shedding.

Goals for this ticket:
- Implement admission thresholding that uses moving-window token refill + burst cap per-customer to avoid single customers exhausting pool credits.
- Add a soft-preemption path: when queue depth or avg wait hits threshold, low-priority requests are gracefully ejected with a structured fallback response and penalty credit, instead of timing out and amplifying retries.
- Introduce a dropback/cooldown circuit-breaker in the scheduler: when prewarm loss or pool loss is detected, reduce admitted concurrency in staged steps and trigger autoscaler with an accelerated scale-up hint.
- Expand observability: new dashboard panels and alerts for inflight_by_pool, prewarm_evictions, avg_queue_wait_95, preemption_events, and backlog_recovery_time.
- Update runbooks and on-call playbook with explicit commands and ownership for rapid capacity cliff mitigation.

Trade-offs considered:
- Hard drops vs soft-preemption: hard drops reduce load faster but surface more immediate 5xxs; we prefer soft-preemption for customer-facing features to return structured fallbacks and avoid cascading retries.
- Aggressive autoscale vs conservative: faster autoscale reduces customer impact but increases cost; we will use accelerated hints only during detected pool-loss events to balance cost.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
1) Admission token refill & burst cap implemented + unit/integration tests.
2) Soft-preemption path implemented for lower-priority request classes with structured response schema and documented client guidance.
3) Circuit-breaker that stages admitted concurrency and fires accelerated scale-up hints created.
4) Dashboards/alerts live and verified (alert runbook linked).
5) Runbook updated and runbook tabletop executed with SRE and on-call.

Owners / action items (concrete):
- Admission throttling implementation (owner: Liam O'Connor, PR: runtime#8421) — due 2026-03-18.
- Soft-preemption flow and client response contract (owner: Naomi Chen, PR: runtime#8446) — due 2026-03-20.
- Circuit-breaker + scale-up hint in autoscaler (owner: Marco Ruiz, PR: infra-autoscaler#304) — due 2026-03-22.
- Dashboards & alerts (owner: Priya Sharma, dashboard PR and alert: grafana#hosted-capacity) — due 2026-03-16.
- Runbook update and tabletop (owner: SRE rotation, doc updated: docs/runbooks/hosted-capacity-dropback) — tabletop scheduled 2026-03-25.

Notes: make sure client SDKs are informed of the new structured fallback response so product teams can implement graceful client-side retries. We will coordinate an announcement and compatibility guide in the Developer Bulletin before releasing soft-preemption widely.
